meta.name: demo-signup-revamp
meta.title: DEMO-12 signup revamp decisions
intro: Only the items still open in the signup revamp are collected here: where social login sits, how the consent screen is arranged, and the wording when a signup finishes.

Each item carries its source and background, and every option says what changes when it is picked. When you are done, press Confirm as requester at the bottom, and the agent goes straight on to the decider page.

decisions.title: Should social login sit on the first screen
decisions.question: Decide whether the first signup screen shows email entry and social login together.
background: Half of the drop-off happens on the first screen. Social login needs no typing, but it adds a step later that links the account to an email one.
Putting social login first shortens the time to a finished signup; keeping only email signup means no account-linking screen has to be built.

options.label: Keep email signup only
options.effect: No account-linking screen, but a signup takes longer to finish

options.label: Put social login first
options.effect: Signup gets faster, but an account-linking screen ships with it

options.label: Put social login below email
options.effect: Email signup leads, but social login is easier to miss

parts.rationale: Cutting the time to a finished signup pays off, and the account-linking screen is built once.

copy_blocks.label: Draft message
copy_blocks.text:
Some items in the DEMO-12 signup revamp are still open.
1) Whether social login goes on the first screen
2) Which screen the consent items are collected on
Please pick them on the page below.

decisions.title: Which screen collects the consent items
decisions.question: Decide whether the required and optional consent items sit on one screen or are split across the flow.
background: This item is not written down anywhere: the screen work stalled here while decision 1 was unresolved.
One screen shortens the flow, while splitting the items makes the first pass feel lighter.

options.label: Collect them on the signup screen
options.effect: One step fewer, but the screen looks long at first glance

options.label: Split them across the flow
options.effect: Lighter per step, but one more step to finish

parts.rationale: There are only three required items, so one screen stays short and saves a step.

decisions.title: Wording when signup finishes, and what a failure rolls back
decisions.question: Decide the wording on the screen after signup and what is rolled back when a signup fails halfway.
background: The same wording goes into the signup email and the screen, so it is hard to change later. The word "Start" already appears on the home screen button.
A signup that fails halfway leaves some of what was entered behind. Decide whether to keep it for a retry or return to the first screen.

parts.label: Finish wording

options.label: You are all set
options.effect: Does not clash with the home button and says the signup is done

options.label: Shall we get started
options.effect: Matches older wording but reads as if signup is not finished

options.label: Welcome
options.effect: Short, but says nothing about what to do next

parts.rationale: It says the signup is done and points at the next step.

parts.label: Failure rollback

options.label: Return to the first screen
options.effect: No trace of the failed attempt is left behind

options.label: Keep it and let the person retry
options.effect: Retrying is quick, but a half-filled state stays behind

parts.rationale: Keeping what was entered saves retrying people from typing the same values again.
